html:
The Second Carib War was a rising in 1795 and 1796 by the Garifuna, or Black Caribs, of St Vincent against British rule, with help from revolutionary France. It was their last war for the island.

The Garifuna descended from Kalinago and Africans who had escaped slavery or shipwreck. British planters wanted their fertile land for sugar. The paramount chief Joseph Chatoyer allied with the French agent Victor Hugues and burned estates across the island.

Chatoyer was killed in March 1795, and British reinforcements forced the Garifuna to surrender in 1796. Most were then deported. Chatoyer is today the first national hero of St Vincent and the Grenadines.
